The Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 31, verses 1–5 (part 1 of 2):

.
His saying: ﴿And We did send messengers before you to their peoples﴾, just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who were criminals﴾, meaning those who committed crimes, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾. This is a report from Allah, glorified is He, that His help for His believing servants is a duty upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not break the appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in honour for His righteous servants. Some reciters paused on ḥaqqan (ﷲ) and made the subject of kāna a pronoun referring to the vengeance, with its predicate being ḥaqqan, meaning: and the vengeance was ḥaqqan (a true obligation).
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: This is weak. The correct reading is that naṣr al-muʾminīn (the help of the believers) is its subject, ḥaqqan is its predicate, and ʿalaynā is related to ḥaqqan, or to an omitted element which is an adjective of it.
﴿Allah is the One who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read yursilu "al-rīḥa" in the singular. The rest read "al-riyāḥ" in the plural. Abū ʿAmr said: Whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a resumptive sentence (mustaʾnafa, a new sentence not grammatically dependent on what precedes it), brought to explain what preceded concerning the states of the winds. Accordingly, the sentence ﴿And We did send﴾ up to His saying ﴿and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it stirs up clouds﴾, meaning it agitates them from wherever they are. ﴿Then He spreads them in the sky as He wills﴾, sometimes moving, sometimes standing still, sometimes covering the sky, sometimes not covering it, sometimes to a great distance and sometimes to a near distance. The explanation of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Baqara and in Surat al-Nūr. ﴿And He makes them into fragments﴾ at another time, or He makes them after spreading them into scattered pieces. Kisaf is the plural of kisfa, and a kisfa is a piece of cloud.
The explanation of it and the variation in its reading have already passed. ﴿Then you see the rain come forth from within it﴾. Al-wadq is the rain, and min khilālihi means from its midst.
Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, meaning with the rain, ﴿whomever He wills of His servants﴾, meaning their lands and their earth, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. Idhā here is the sudden idhā (idhā al-fujā'iyya, which marks a sudden occurrence), meaning they suddenly rejoiced at the arrival of the rain. Istibshār means joy.
﴿And although they were, before it was sent down upon them﴾, meaning before the rain was sent down upon them. Wa-in here is the light form (mukhaffafa, the light form of inna) and in it is an omitted dummy pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was, they were before it was sent down upon them. His saying ﴿before it﴾ is a repetition for emphasis, as al-Akhfash and most grammarians said, as al-Naḥḥās related from them.
Qutrub said: The pronoun in qablihi refers to the rain, meaning: and although they were before the sending down, before the rain.
It was said: The meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and rain. It was said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, meaning before seeing them (p-1138), and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.
It was said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it was said: to the sending, and it was said: to the rejoicing.
The preponderant view is the first, and all the others are in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of kāna is ﴿despairing﴾, meaning hopeless or despondent. The discussion of this has already been verified.
﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy﴾, which arise from the sending down of the rain: the plants, fruits and crops by which fertility and ease of life come about. That is: look with the gaze of reflection and insight, so that you may infer from it the oneness of Allah and His unique authorship of this wondrous work.
The majority read "athari" in the singular. Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿āthār﴾ in the plural. ﴿How He gives life to the earth after its death﴾. The subject of the giving of life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He. It was said: it refers to the trace. This sentence is in a place of accusative governed by unẓur (look), meaning: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.
Al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywa read tuḥyī with the feminine prefix, its subject being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the traces according to the reading of those who read the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ is to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in Majesty, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is surely the Giver of life to the dead﴾, meaning He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, meaning of great and abundant power.
﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellowed﴾. The pronoun in faraʾūhu refers to the crops and plants which were from the trace of Allah's mercy, meaning: they saw them yellowed from the cold arising from the wind which Allah sent after they had turned green.
It was said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.
It was said: it refers to the trace indicated by the traces.
It was said: it refers to the cloud, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more appropriate.
The lām is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-muwaṭṭi'a, the lām that prepares for an oath), and the answer of the oath is ﴿they would surely continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and it takes the place of the answer of the condition.
The meaning: And if We sent a wind, hot or cold, and it struck their crop with yellowing, they would surely continue after that to disbelieve in Allah and deny His blessings. In this is evidence of the swiftness of their change, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, and this is not the state of the people of faith.
Then He likened them to the dead and the deaf, saying: ﴿So indeed you cannot make the dead hear﴾ when you call them, and likewise these, because of their lack of understanding of the realities and their ignorance of what is right. ﴿Nor can you make the deaf hear the call﴾ when you call them to the truth and admonish them with the admonitions of Allah, and remind them of the Hereafter and what is in it. His saying ﴿when they turn away retreating﴾ is an explanation of their aversion from the truth after the explanation that they are like the dead and that they are deaf in their ears. The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Naml.
Then He described them as blind, saying: ﴿And you cannot guide the blind away from their error﴾, because they lack benefit from sight as it should be, or because they lack insight ﴿You can make none hear except those who believe in Our signs﴾, meaning you make none hear except these, because they are people of reflection, contemplation, and inference from traces to the One who makes the traces. ﴿So they are Muslims﴾, meaning they submit to the truth and follow it.
﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness﴾. Glorified is He mentions another proof of His perfect power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "from weakness" is: from a drop (nuṭfa).
Al-Wāḥidī said: The exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one who is weak.
It was said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the physique grows until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, meaning in old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. Shayba is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.
The majority read ḍuʿf with a ḍamma on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with a fatḥa. al-Jaḥdarī read it with a fatḥa in the first two and a ḍamma in the third.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The ḍamma is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm. Al-Jawharī said: ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf are the opposite of strength. It was said: it is with a fatḥa in opinion and with a ḍamma in the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ in His management, ﴿the All-Powerful﴾ over creating what He wills. The Kufans permitted min ḍaʿfin with a fatḥa on the ḍād and the ʿayn.
﴿And the day the Hour is established﴾, meaning the Resurrection, and it was named "the Hour" because it is established at the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they did not remain but an hour﴾, meaning they will swear that they remained in the world or in their graves only an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay, and this settled in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking that their oath corresponded to reality.
Ibn Qutayba said: They lied at this time as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure, and if they meant their stay in the graves, they swore out of ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh (intermediate state). ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: afaka al-rajul, when a man turns away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the same way of turning away they were turned away.
It was said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth. It was said: from good. The first is more appropriate, and this is evidence that their oath is a lie.
﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. There has been disagreement about specifying those who were given knowledge. It was said: the angels. It was said: the prophets. It was said: the scholars of the nations. It was said: the believers of this nation. There is no obstacle to carrying it upon all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and His decree. Al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
Al-Wāḥidī said: The exegetes took this to be by way of advancing and delaying, with the assumed sense: And those who were given knowledge said, in the Book of Allah. The response of those who were given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in return for their oath with an oath. Then they alerted them, by way of rebuke, that this "time" in which they found themselves is ﴿the Day of Resurrection, but you used not to know﴾ that it is true, rather you used to hasten it in denial and mockery.
﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾, meaning their apology will not benefit them on that Day, nor will their knowledge of the Resurrection profit them.
It was said: when the believers refuted them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.
The majority read "lā tanfaʿu" with the feminine prefix. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with the masculine prefix. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It is said: istaʿtabtuhu fa-aʿtabanī, meaning I asked him to be pleased and he was pleased with me. This is when you were the one who had wronged him. The literal sense of aʿtabtuhu is that I removed his displeasure. The meaning is: they are not called to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called to that in the world.
﴿And We have certainly set forth for people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾, meaning every kind of example among the parables by which they are guided to the oneness of Allah and the truthfulness of His messengers, and We have argued against them with every argument that shows the falsehood of polytheism. ﴿And if you bring them a sign﴾ from the signs of the Qur'an that speak to that, or if you bring them a sign like the staff and the hand, ﴿those who disbelieve will surely say: You are nothing but falsifiers﴾, meaning: you, O Muhammad, and your companions are nothing but falsifiers, adherents of falsehoods, following magic and what resembles it in falsehood.
﴿Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of those who do not know﴾, meaning in the same way, that sealing, Allah seals over the hearts of those who lack beneficial knowledge by which they are guided to the truth and saved from falsehood.
Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded His prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to be patient, giving as the reason the truth of Allah's promise and the impossibility of its breaking. He said: ﴿So be patient﴾ regarding what you hear from them of harm and what you expect from them of disbelieving acts. Indeed Allah has promised you victory over them and the elevation of your proof and the manifestation of your call, and His promise is true, with no breaking of it. ﴿And let not those who have no certainty make you impatient﴾, meaning do not let them bring you to levity, and do not let them provoke you away from your religion and what you are upon, those who do not have certainty in Allah and do not believe His prophets and do not believe in His books. The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. It is said: istakhaffa fulānun fulānan, meaning he found him foolish until he led him to follow him in error.
The majority read "yastakhiffannaka" with the unpointed kh (khā' mu'jama) and the f. Yaʿqūb and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read it with an unpointed ḥ (ḥāʾ muhmala) and a q, from al-istiḥqāq (to be entitled to or to belittle). The prohibition in the verse is of the type of: "lā arayannaka hāhunā" (I should not find you here).

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim defends the honour of his brother except that it is a right upon Allah to protect him from the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection." Then he recited: ﴿And it was upon Us to help the believers.﴾ This narration is through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda'.

Abu Ya'la and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from him regarding His words: ﴿And He makes it fragments,﴾ he said: pieces, some of them upon others. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾ he said: the rain. ﴿Coming out from within it﴾ he said: from among it.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call,﴾ concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling out to the people of Badr. The chain of transmission is weak.

What is well known in the Sahihayn (the two authentic collections, Bukhari and Muslim) and others is that 'A'isha used this verse to reject the report of some Companions that the Prophet (ﷺ) "called out to the people of the well of Badr." This is an instance of using the general (al-'amm) to reject the specific (al-khass), for the Prophet (ﷺ) said when it was said to him, "You are calling out to decaying bodies": "You are no more able to hear what I say than they are." In Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) calling out to them, said: "O Messenger of Allah, are you calling to them after three days, and can they hear? Allah says, ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear.﴾" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you are no more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to answer."

His saying: ﴿And We did send messengers before you to their peoples﴾, just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who were criminals﴾, meaning those who committed crimes, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾. This is a report from Allah, glorified is He, that His help for His believing servants is a duty upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not break the appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in honour for His righteous servants. Some reciters paused on ḥaqqan (ﷲ) and made the subject of kāna a pronoun referring to the vengeance, with its predicate being ḥaqqan, meaning: and the vengeance was ḥaqqan (a true obligation).
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: This is weak. The correct reading is that naṣr al-muʾminīn (the help of the believers) is its subject, ḥaqqan is its predicate, and ʿalaynā is related to ḥaqqan, or to an omitted element which is an adjective of it.
﴿Allah is the One who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read yursilu "al-rīḥa" in the singular. The rest read "al-riyāḥ" in the plural. Abū ʿAmr said: Whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a resumptive sentence (mustaʾnafa, a new sentence not grammatically dependent on what precedes it), brought to explain what preceded concerning the states of the winds. Accordingly, the sentence ﴿And We did send﴾ up to His saying ﴿and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it stirs up clouds﴾, meaning it agitates them from wherever they are. ﴿Then He spreads them in the sky as He wills﴾, sometimes moving, sometimes standing still, sometimes covering the sky, sometimes not covering it, sometimes to a great distance and sometimes to a near distance. The explanation of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Baqara and in Surat al-Nūr. ﴿And He makes them into fragments﴾ at another time, or He makes them after spreading them into scattered pieces. Kisaf is the plural of kisfa, and a kisfa is a piece of cloud.
The explanation of it and the variation in its reading have already passed. ﴿Then you see the rain come forth from within it﴾. Al-wadq is the rain, and min khilālihi means from its midst.
Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, meaning with the rain, ﴿whomever He wills of His servants﴾, meaning their lands and their earth, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. ﴿And although they were, before it was sent down upon them﴾, meaning before the rain was sent down upon them. Wa-in here is the light form (mukhaffafa, the light form of inna) and in it is an omitted dummy pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was, they were before it was sent down upon them. His saying ﴿before it﴾ is a repetition for emphasis, as al-Akhfash and most grammarians said, as al-Naḥḥās related from them.
Qutrub said: The pronoun in qablihi refers to the rain, meaning: and although they were before the sending down, before the rain.
It was said: The meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and rain. It was said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, meaning before seeing them (p-1138), and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.
It was said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it was said: to the sending, and it was said: to the rejoicing.
The preponderant view is the first, and all the others are in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of kāna is ﴿despairing﴾, meaning hopeless or despondent. The discussion of this has already been verified.
﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy﴾, which arise from the sending down of the rain: the plants, fruits and crops by which fertility and ease of life come about. That is: look with the gaze of reflection and insight, so that you may infer from it the oneness of Allah and His unique authorship of this wondrous work.
The majority read "athari" in the singular. Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿āthār﴾ in the plural. ﴿How He gives life to the earth after its death﴾. The subject of the giving of life is a pronoun referring to Allah, glorified is He. It was said: it refers to the trace. This sentence is in a place of accusative governed by unẓur (look), meaning: look at the manner of this wondrous giving of life to the earth.
Al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Ḥaywa read tuḥyī with the feminine prefix, its subject being a pronoun referring to the mercy, or to the traces according to the reading of those who read the plural. The indication in His saying ﴿Indeed that﴾ is to Allah, glorified is He, meaning: indeed Allah, the Mighty in Majesty, who originated these mentioned things, ﴿is surely the Giver of life to the dead﴾, meaning He is capable of reviving them in the Hereafter, resurrecting them and recompensing them, just as He revived the dead earth with rain. ﴿And He is over all things Powerful﴾, meaning of great and abundant power.

It was said: it refers to the wind, and it may be masculine or feminine.
It was said: it refers to the trace indicated by the traces.
It was said: it refers to the cloud, because when it is yellow it does not rain. The first is more appropriate.
The lām is the preparatory lām (al-lām al-muwaṭṭi'a, the lām that prepares for an oath), and the answer of the oath is ﴿they would surely continue after it to disbelieve﴾, and it takes the place of the answer of the condition.

In this is evidence of the swiftness of their change, their lack of patience, and the weakness of their hearts, and this is not the state of the people of faith.

The explanation of this has already passed in Surat al-Naml.

﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness﴾. Glorified is He mentions another proof of His perfect power, which is the creation of man himself in various stages. The meaning of "from weakness" is: from a drop (nuṭfa).
Al-Wāḥidī said: The exegetes said: from a drop, and the meaning is: from one who is weak.
It was said: the intended meaning is the state of infancy and childhood. ﴿Then He made after weakness strength﴾, which is the strength of youth, for at that time strength becomes firm and the physique grows until it reaches its completion. ﴿Then He made after strength weakness﴾, meaning in old age and senility. ﴿And white hair﴾. Shayba is the completion of weakness and the extreme of old age.
The majority read ḍuʿf with a ḍamma on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with a fatḥa. al-Jaḥdarī read it with a fatḥa in the first two and a ḍamma in the third.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The ḍamma is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm. Al-Jawharī said: ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf are the opposite of strength. It was said: it is with a fatḥa in opinion and with a ḍamma in the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ in His management, ﴿the All-Powerful﴾ over creating what He wills. The Kufans permitted min ḍaʿfin with a fatḥa on the ḍād and the ʿayn.
﴿And the day the Hour is established﴾, meaning the Resurrection, and it was named "the Hour" because it is established at the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they did not remain but an hour﴾, meaning they will swear that they remained in the world or in their graves only an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay, and this settled in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking that their oath corresponded to reality.
Ibn Qutayba said: They lied at this time as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure, and if they meant their stay in the graves, they swore out of ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh (intermediate state). ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: afaka al-rajul, when a man turns away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the same way of turning away they were turned away.
It was said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth. It was said: from good. The first is more appropriate, and this is evidence that their oath is a lie.
﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. It was said: the believers of this nation. There is no obstacle to carrying it upon all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and His decree. Al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

It was said: when the believers refuted them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.

The majority read ḍuʿf with a ḍamma on the ḍād in these places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with a fatḥa. al-Jaḥdarī read it with a fatḥa in the first two and a ḍamma in the third.
Al-Farrāʾ said: The ḍamma is the dialect of Quraysh and the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm. Al-Jawharī said: ḍaʿf and ḍuʿf are the opposite of strength. It was said: it is with a fatḥa in opinion and with a ḍamma in the body. ﴿He creates what He wills﴾, meaning from all things, and among them strength and weakness in the children of Adam. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ in His management, ﴿the All-Powerful﴾ over creating what He wills. The Kufans permitted min ḍaʿfin with a fatḥa on the ḍād and the ʿayn.
﴿And the day the Hour is established﴾, meaning the Resurrection, and it was named "the Hour" because it is established at the last hour of the hours of this world. ﴿The criminals will swear that they did not remain but an hour﴾, meaning they will swear that they remained in the world or in their graves only an hour. It is possible that they belittled the duration of their stay, and this settled in their minds, so they swore to it while thinking that their oath corresponded to reality.
Ibn Qutayba said: They lied at this time as they used to lie before. This is the apparent meaning, because if they meant their stay in the world, each of them knows its measure, and if they meant their stay in the graves, they swore out of ignorance, if they do not know the times in the barzakh (intermediate state). ﴿Thus they were turned away﴾. It is said: afaka al-rajul, when a man turns away from truthfulness. So the meaning is: in the same way of turning away they were turned away.
It was said: the intended meaning is that they were turned away from the truth. It was said: from good. The first is more appropriate, and this is evidence that their oath is a lie.
﴿And those who were given knowledge and faith will say: Indeed you remained in the Book of Allah until the Day of Resurrection﴾. There has been disagreement about specifying those who were given knowledge. It was said: the angels. It was said: the prophets. It was said: the scholars of the nations. It was said: the believers of this nation. There is no obstacle to carrying it upon all of them. The meaning of "in the Book of Allah" is: in His knowledge and His decree. Al-Zajjāj said: in the knowledge of Allah recorded in the Preserved Tablet.
Al-Wāḥidī said: The exegetes took this to be by way of advancing and delaying, with the assumed sense: And those who were given knowledge said, in the Book of Allah. The response of those who were given knowledge to them was with an oath for emphasis, or in return for their oath with an oath. Then they alerted them, by way of rebuke, that this "time" in which they found themselves is ﴿the Day of Resurrection, but you used not to know﴾ that it is true, rather you used to hasten it in denial and mockery.
﴿So on that Day, their excuse will not benefit those who did wrong﴾, meaning their apology will not benefit them on that Day, nor will their knowledge of the Resurrection profit them.
It was said: when the believers refuted them, they asked to return to the world and offered excuses, but they were not accepted.
The majority read "lā tanfaʿu" with the feminine prefix. ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read it with the masculine prefix. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. It is said: istaʿtabtuhu fa-aʿtabanī, meaning I asked him to be pleased and he was pleased with me. This is when you were the one who had wronged him. The literal sense of aʿtabtuhu is that I removed his displeasure. The meaning is: they are not called to remove their displeasure through repentance and obedience, as they were called to that in the world.

Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abu al-Darda', who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No Muslim defends the honour of his brother except that it is a right upon Allah to protect him from the Fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection." Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed, ﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call,﴾ concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) calling out to the people of Badr. His saying: ﴿And We did send messengers before you to their peoples﴾, just as We sent you to your people, ﴿and they came to them with clear proofs﴾, meaning with miracles and luminous arguments. ﴿Then We took vengeance on those who were criminals﴾, meaning those who committed crimes, which are sins. ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾. This is a report from Allah, glorified is He, that His help for His believing servants is a duty upon Him, and He is true to His promise and does not break the appointment. In it is an honouring of the believers and an increase in honour for His righteous servants. Some reciters paused on ḥaqqan (ﷲ) and made the subject of kāna a pronoun referring to the vengeance, with its predicate being ḥaqqan, meaning: and the vengeance was ḥaqqan (a true obligation).
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: This is weak. The correct reading is that naṣr al-muʾminīn (the help of the believers) is its subject, ḥaqqan is its predicate, and ʿalaynā is related to ḥaqqan, or to an omitted element which is an adjective of it.
﴿Allah is the One who sends the winds﴾. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn Muḥaysin read yursilu "al-rīḥa" in the singular. The rest read "al-riyāḥ" in the plural. Abū ʿAmr said: Whatever has the meaning of mercy is plural, and whatever has the meaning of punishment is singular. This sentence is a resumptive sentence (mustaʾnafa, a new sentence not grammatically dependent on what precedes it), brought to explain what preceded concerning the states of the winds. Accordingly, the sentence ﴿And We did send﴾ up to His saying ﴿and it was incumbent upon Us to help the believers﴾ is a parenthetical insertion. ﴿So it stirs up clouds﴾, meaning it agitates them from wherever they are. ﴿Then He spreads them in the sky as He wills﴾, sometimes moving, sometimes standing still, sometimes covering the sky, sometimes not covering it, sometimes to a great distance and sometimes to a near distance. The explanation of this verse has already passed in Surat al-Baqara and in Surat al-Nūr. ﴿And He makes them into fragments﴾ at another time, or He makes them after spreading them into scattered pieces. Kisaf is the plural of kisfa, and a kisfa is a piece of cloud.
The explanation of it and the variation in its reading have already passed. ﴿Then you see the rain come forth from within it﴾. Al-wadq is the rain, and min khilālihi means from its midst.
Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read "yakhruju min khalalihi". ﴿Then when He strikes with it﴾, meaning with the rain, ﴿whomever He wills of His servants﴾, meaning their lands and their earth, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. ﴿And although they were, before it was sent down upon them﴾, meaning before the rain was sent down upon them. Wa-in here is the light form (mukhaffafa, the light form of inna) and in it is an omitted dummy pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr shaʾn) which is its subject, meaning: and indeed the matter was, they were before it was sent down upon them. His saying ﴿before it﴾ is a repetition for emphasis, as al-Akhfash and most grammarians said, as al-Naḥḥās related from them.
Qutrub said: The pronoun in qablihi refers to the rain, meaning: and although they were before the sending down, before the rain.
It was said: The meaning is: before the sending down of the rain upon them, before the crops and rain. It was said: before it descended upon them from before the clouds, meaning before seeing them (p-1138), and al-Naḥḥās chose this view.
It was said: the pronoun refers to the fragments (kisaf), and it was said: to the sending, and it was said: to the rejoicing.
The preponderant view is the first, and all the others are in extreme artificiality and forced interpretation. The predicate of kāna is ﴿despairing﴾, meaning hopeless or despondent. The discussion of this has already been verified.
﴿So look at the traces of Allah's mercy﴾, which arise from the sending down of the rain: the plants, fruits and crops by which fertility and ease of life come about. Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 31, verses 6–11 (part 1 of 2):

It is Meccan (*Makkiyya*, revealed in Mecca) except for three verses, which are His saying: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens﴾ [Luqman 31:27], through to the end of the three verses. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, as transmitted by al-Nahhas from him. Ibn al-Durays, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Dala'il* also transmitted from him that it is Meccan without any exception. Al-Qurtubi reported from Qatada that it is Meccan except for two verses.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah transmitted from al-Bara', who said: "We used to pray behind the Prophet (ﷺ) at the noon prayer, and we would hear from him verse after verse of Surat Luqman and al-Dhariyat."

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿Alif Lam Mim. These are the verses of the Book﴾. The discussion of the like of the opening of this surah, and its place in grammatical analysis (*i'rab*), has already been covered fully, so we will not repeat it. Also the explanation of what the demonstrative refers to.

As for "*al-Hakim*" (the All-Wise), it may be in the sense of *mufil* (causing), or in the sense of *fa'il* (agent), or in the sense of "possessor of wisdom," or "the one who is wise in His speech."

﴿Guidance and mercy﴾ are accusative as circumstantial complements (*hal*) according to the reading of the majority.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "These are the verses of the Book while being guidance and mercy." Hamza read "*wa rahmatun*" with a nominative ending, making them the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "it is guidance and mercy." It is also permissible that they be predicates of "these" (*tilka*). The "*muhsin*" (the one who does good) is the one who performs good deeds, or the one who worships Allah as if he sees Him, as was established from him (ﷺ) in the Sahih when Jibril asked him about *ihsan* (excellence). He said: "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you."

Then He explained the deeds of the good-doers, saying: ﴿Those who establish the prayer, and give the zakat, and they are certain of the Hereafter﴾. The relative pronoun is in the genitive position as a description of "*al-muhsinin*," or in the nominative or accusative position as an expression of praise or a break (*qat'*). He singled out these three acts of worship because they are the pillars of worship.

﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful﴾. Its explanation has already been given at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara. The meaning here is that those who are characterized by excellence and performing those acts of obedience which are the foundations of worship are upon the path of guidance.

They are the ones who attain their aims, who triumph with the good of both abodes.

﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾. The position of "*wa min al-nas*" is nominative, as a beginning (*ibtida'*), as already explained in Surat al-Baqara. Its predicate is ﴿one who purchases idle talk﴾. "*Man*" is either a relative pronoun or a qualifying noun. "*Lahw al-hadith*" (idle talk) is everything that distracts from good, such as singing, entertainments, and false narratives, and everything that is objectionable. The construction is explanatory (*idafa bayaniyya*).

It has been said: what is meant is buying singing slave-girls and male singers, so the implied meaning is: "and whoever buys people of idle talk."

Al-Hasan said: *lahw al-hadith* is musical instruments and singing. It is also reported from him that he said: it is disbelief and polytheism.

Al-Qurtubi said: the best of what has been said on this subject is interpreting *lahw al-hadith* as singing, and he said: this is the view of the Companions and the Successors.

The "*lam*" in ﴿so that he may mislead from the way of Allah﴾ is causal (*lil-ta'lil*).

The majority read "*li-yudilla*" with a dammah on the *ya'*, meaning: that he may mislead others from the path of guidance and the method of truth. When he misleads others, he has himself gone astray.

Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn Muhaysin, Humayd, Warsh, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a fatha on the *ya'*, meaning: that he himself may go astray.

They are the ones who attain their aims, who triumph with the good of both abodes.

Its predicate is ﴿one who purchases idle talk﴾. "*Man*" is either a relative pronoun or a qualifying noun. "*Lahw al-hadith*" (idle talk) is everything that distracts from good, such as singing, entertainments, and false narratives, and everything that is objectionable. The construction is explanatory (*idafa bayaniyya*).

It has been said: what is meant is buying singing slave-girls and male singers, so the implied meaning is: "and whoever buys people of idle talk."

Al-Hasan said: *lahw al-hadith* is musical instruments and singing. It is also reported from him that he said: it is disbelief and polytheism.

Al-Qurtubi said: the best of what has been said on this subject is interpreting *lahw al-hadith* as singing, and he said: this is the view of the Companions and the Successors.

Whoever reads with a fatha on the *ya'*, its meaning is that his affair ends in misguidance. Even if he does not purchase it for the sake of misguidance, his affair ends in that. This is supported by the occasion of revelation of the verse, which will come.

Only Ibrahim ibn Sa'd and 'Abdullah al-'Anbari differed from the majority.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: it is permissible for a man to listen to the singing of his slave-girl, since nothing of her is forbidden to him, neither outwardly nor inwardly. How then can he be prevented from enjoying her voice?

I say: I have compiled a treatise containing the statements of the people of knowledge on singing, and what those who permit it and those who forbid it used as evidence. I have verified this matter in a way that one who examines it and reflects on its meanings will not need to look at anything else. Whoever wishes to verify the matter as it should be should refer to it.

The wording of Ibn Jarir is: "It is singing, by Allah, than whom there is no god but He," repeating it three times.

It was concerning such a case that this verse was revealed: ﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾ to the end of the verse. In its chain is 'Ubayd ibn Zahr, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, and there is weakness among them.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya in *Dhamm al-Malahi* and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from 'A'isha, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden the singing-girl, her sale, her price, teaching her, and listening to her," then he recited ﴿And among people is one who purchases idle talk﴾.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Sunan* transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Singing produces hypocrisy in the heart just as water produces herbage." They also transmitted it from him as a statement of Ibn Mas'ud (mawquf).

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Umama that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one raises his voice with singing except that Allah sends to him two devils who sit on his shoulders, striking his chest with their heels until he stops."

There are hadiths on this subject, and each of them has some criticism leveled against it.

Al-Bayhaqi related in *Shu'ab al-Iman* from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿And among mankind is one who purchases idle talk﴾, that he said: "It is a man who buys a slave girl who sings night and day."

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abd Allah ibn Umar that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, regarding His words ﴿And among mankind is one who purchases idle talk﴾: "That refers only to a man buying play and falsehood."

Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Bayhaqi related from Nafi', who said: "I was walking with Abd Allah ibn Umar on a road when he heard the sound of a flute. He put his two fingers in his ears, then turned aside from the road, and kept saying, 'O Nafi', do you hear it?' I said, 'No.' Then he removed his fingers from his ears and said, 'This is what I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do.'"

Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have only been forbidden from two foolish, sinful sounds: a sound at the strain of amusement and the flutes of Satan, and a sound at a calamity, the scratching of faces, the tearing of garments, and the wailing of Satan."

The construction is explanatory (*idafa bayaniyya*).

It has been said: what is meant is buying singing slave-girls and male singers, so the implied meaning is: "and whoever buys people of idle talk."

Al-Hasan said: *lahw al-hadith* is musical instruments and singing. It is also reported from him that he said: it is disbelief and polytheism.

Al-Qurtubi said: the best of what has been said on this subject is interpreting *lahw al-hadith* as singing, and he said: this is the view of the Companions and the Successors.

This is supported by the occasion of revelation of the verse, which will come.

Al-Qurtubi said: the scholars of the regions have agreed on the disapproval of singing and its prohibition.

Only Ibrahim ibn Sa'd and 'Abdullah al-'Anbari differed from the majority.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi said: it is permissible for a man to listen to the singing of his slave-girl, since nothing of her is forbidden to him, neither outwardly nor inwardly. How then can he be prevented from enjoying her voice?

I say: I have compiled a treatise containing the statements of the people of knowledge on singing, and what those who permit it and those who forbid it used as evidence. I have verified this matter in a way that one who examines it and reflects on its meanings will not need to look at anything else. I named it *Ibtal Da'wa al-Ijma' 'ala Tahrim Mutlaq al-Sama'* (Refuting the Claim of Consensus on the Absolute Prohibition of Listening). Whoever wishes to verify the matter as it should be should refer to it.

The position of ﴿without knowledge﴾ is accusative as a circumstantial complement, meaning: while being ignorant of the state of what he buys, or of the state of what benefits and harms in trade. Therefore he exchanges the good for what is pure evil.

It has been said the nominative is a resumption (*isti'naf*). The accusative pronoun in "*yattakhidha-ha*" refers to the verses mentioned previously. The first view is preferable.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and al-A'mash read "*wa yattakhidha-ha*" with an accusative ending, coordinated with "*yudilla*." The accusative pronoun refers to "the way." The plural is by consideration of its meaning, just as the singular in the two verbs is by consideration of its wording. The meaning of "*bath*" (dispersal) has already been explained. ﴿And We sent down from the sky water, and We caused to grow therein from every noble pair﴾, i.e., We sent down rain from the sky and caused to grow therein, by means of its descent, from every pair, i.e., every kind. He described it as "noble" for the beauty of its color and the abundance of its benefits.

It has been said that what is meant by this is people, so the noble among them is the one who goes to Paradise, and the base one is the one who goes to the Fire. This was said by al-Sha'bi and others, but the first view is preferable.

The reference in "*hadha*" (this) is to what was mentioned about the creation of the heavens and the earth. It is the subject, and its predicate is ﴿the creation of Allah﴾, i.e., His creation. ﴿Then show me what those beside Him have created﴾ of your gods that you worship. The interrogation is for rebuke and reproach. The meaning is: show me what they have created of anything that resembles or approximates the creation of Allah. This command to them is for the purpose of incapacitating and silencing them.

Then He turned away from rebuking them with what was mentioned to a judgment against them of misguidance (p. 1141), clear and evident. He said: ﴿But the wrongdoers are in manifest error.﴾ He established their wrong first and their misguidance second, and described their misguidance as obvious and manifest. Whoever is like this does not understand the proof nor is guided to the truth.
